requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute with an optional `SurrogateType` property. When a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>` carries the attribute, the source generator writes the formatter body into that class. The type `T` may live in an assembly with no MessagePack reference. With no surrogate, every public read-write instance member of `T` is serialized under its name as a string key (contractless). With a surrogate, the surrogate's `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes set the keys and which members are serialized. The change also adds four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–MsgPack022), reuses several existing ones, and excludes these formatters from the hand-written formatter scan. Both formatter templates now emit `partial class` for these formatters. Execution tests use a new test assembly with no MessagePack reference.
story.why: REQ-2129 asks for a source-generated formatter, declared in Project B, for a type that lives in a dependency-free Project A. The requirement offered three options for supplying keys (DataMember, user-copied attributes, generated attributes). The agent chose none of them: it used contractless-by-default plus a surrogate type instead. Unions are explicitly unsupported.

findings.description: Claim C11 disputed: IsPublicReadWrite at GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L279-281 includes init-only properties (SetMethod.IsInitOnly == true), which are not read-write, while GetInstanceMembers at L267 combined with property.SetMethod at L281 skips public read-write virtual properties when a derived class overrides only get (SetMethod is null on the overriding IPropertySymbol in Roslyn). Also, none of the four named tests exercise base-type members.

Claim C12 disputed: The named test SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership does not test unlisted members of T or string keys in surrogate mode: ExternalWidget has Id, Name, and Internal (ExternalWidget.cs L9-14), and ExternalWidgetSurrogate (GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypes.cs L27-37) lists all three, excluding Internal via [IgnoreMember] rather than omitting it, and uses only int keys 3 and 7.

Claim C13 disputed: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L190 delegates to IsPublicReadWrite (L279-281), which accepts init-only properties on T (not read-write) and rejects public read-write virtual properties where T overrides only get; in addition, neither named test exercises the !IsPublicReadWrite(target) branch of L190.

Claim C16 disputed: Explicit IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver detection at GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L84-85 is broken: in Roslyn C#, an explicit interface implementation IMethodSymbol has m.Name prefixed with the interface name (e.g. 'MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize'), never 'OnBeforeSerialize', so m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0 && (m.Name == 'OnBeforeSerialize' || m.Name == 'OnAfterDeserialize') is always false. Also type.GetMembers() misses explicit implementations on base classes, and none of the named tests cover callbacks, init, or required members.

The template emits `sealed partial class` but the checked-in compiled FormatterTemplate.cs (line 34) emits `partial class`. Regenerating the T4 output would silently change the generated code and add `sealed` to user formatters. S1 passes only because both files changed.

GetInstanceMembers(surrogate) includes non-public fields and properties of the surrogate. Any private helper member without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] triggers MemberNeedsKey and blocks generation, which the docs do not mention.

The record is public, and it carries ISymbol values through the incremental pipeline. That roots compilations and defeats incremental caching. Diagnostics are also computed by running Collect a second time (MessagePackGenerator.cs L125).
The feature is excluded from the force-map-mode execution tests. Int-key surrogate formatters under ForceMap are therefore never run.

The project targets net8.0 only. If ExecutionTests multi-targets (for example, a .NET Framework target), this ProjectReference would fail for the other targets. The ExecutionTests target frameworks are not visible in the diff.

Several rejection paths have no test: the missing-parameterless-constructor check, the generic-type, struct-kind and accessibility branches of MsgPack021, duplicate surrogate keys, and MemberNeedsKey.

Explicit IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver detection is always false: in Roslyn, an explicit interface implementation method has m.Name prefixed with the interface name (e.g. 'MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize'), not 'OnBeforeSerialize' (which is on m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations[0].Name). Also type.GetMembers() ignores base classes, and sharing one needsCast flag for both callbacks can box structs unnecessarily. For any type with explicit callback implementations, the generated formatter omits the interface cast and fails to compile with CS1061.

IsPartial only checks whether the formatter class itself has a declaration with the partial keyword and never checks symbol.ContainingType (contrary to doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md L26). A partial formatter nested inside a non-partial type skips MsgPack019 and emits a partial wrapper for the outer type, failing compilation with CS0260.

Collect validates the target data type T for generic parameters, abstractness, and accessibility, but does not validate the formatter class itself. If the user-declared formatter is generic, abstract, or private inside a containing class, no MsgPack diagnostic is reported and GeneratedMessagePackResolver emits uncompilable instantiation code (CS0305, CS0144, or CS0122).

CreateSurrogateMembers checks 'key is not (int or string)' without rejecting negative integer keys (e.g. [Key(-1)]). Negative int keys pass validation and produce MemberSerializationInfo with IntKey < 0, breaking int-key array formatter generation.

Extracting SurrogateType via 'as INamedTypeSymbol' silently turns non-named types (such as typeof(int[])) into null, causing the generator to silently emit a contractless formatter instead of reporting an invalid surrogate diagnostic; unbound generic surrogate types (typeof(MySurrogate<>)) are also not rejected.

FullModel.ObjectInfos is an ImmutableSortedSet<ObjectSerializationInfo> ordered by ResolverRegisterInfo.CompareTo (DataType). If two [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes target the same type T (or one targets a [MessagePackObject] type), one ObjectSerializationInfo is silently dropped during model union, leaving the second partial formatter class without generated Serialize/Deserialize methods (CS0535).
GeneratedFormatterCollector passes isIntKey directly from surrogate [Key(int)] annotations without consulting ForceMapMode in AnalyzerOptions, so int-key surrogates ignore force-map mode.

Structs skip the accessible parameterless constructor check, but in C# 10+ a struct in a referenced assembly can declare a private or internal parameterless constructor, causing the generated 'new T()' call to fail with CS0122 instead of reporting NoDeserializingConstructor.
